q: When a capacitor is connected to a battery, the two conductors have charges of equal magnitude and _____ signs.
e: When a capacitor is connected to a battery, the two conductors have charges of equal magnitude and opposite signs. identical is not opposite, and neutral is not opposite either. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field. A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy and holds a pd at its terminals.

q: The magnitude of the charge on each conductor, Q, is called the _____ of the capacitor.
e: The magnitude of the charge on each conductor, Q, is called the charge of the capacitor. capacitance is not charge, and potential is not charge either. The plates must conduct so charge can spread; the gap must insulate or the field collapses. A conductor lets charge drift when a potential difference is applied across it.

q: The quantity of charge Q on the capacitor is linearly proportional to the _____ V between the conductors.
e: The quantity of charge Q on the capacitor is linearly proportional to the potential difference V between the conductors. current is not potential difference, and resistance is not potential difference either. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field.

q: The relationship between charge and potential difference of a capacitor can be written as _____.
e: The relationship between charge and potential difference of a capacitor can be written as Q=CV. Put Q=C/V or Q=V/C in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Potential difference is the electrical push between two points; no push, no current.

q: The capacitance of a capacitor is defined as the ratio of the _____ to the potential difference of the capacitor.
e: The capacitance of a capacitor is defined as the ratio of the charge to the potential difference of the capacitor. current and resistance belong to other processes, not this charge case. Charge is conserved; it is what a current carries and what a capacitor stores on its plates.

q: In the SI system, the unit of capacitance is _____.
e: In the SI system, the unit of capacitance is farad. coulomb is not farad, and volt is not farad either. One farad is one coulomb per volt, so practical capacitors are µF, nF or pF.
Therefore 1 F is equivalent to 1 C V^-1. Put 1 A s^-1 or 1 J C^-1 in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. One farad is one coulomb per volt, so practical capacitors are µF, nF or pF.

q: The unit farad is named in honor of _____.
e: The unit farad is named in honor of Michael Faraday. Put Isaac Newton or Albert Einstein in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Faraday's law: induced emf equals the rate of change of magnetic flux through the loop. One farad is one coulomb per volt, so practical capacitors are µF, nF or pF.

q: The farad is a very _____ unit of capacitance.
e: The farad is a very large unit of capacitance. Put small or medium in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. One farad is one coulomb per volt, so practical capacitors are µF, nF or pF.
1 microfarad (µ F) is equal to 10^-6 F. Put 10^-9 F or 10^-12 F in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. A microfarad is 10^-6 F, the usual electrolytic size.
1 nanofarad (nF) is equal to 10^-9 F. Put 10^-6 F or 10^-12 F in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. A nanofarad is 10^-9 F, a thousand times smaller than a microfarad.
1 picofarad (pF) is equal to 10^-12 F. 10^-6 F is not 10^-12 F, and 10^-9 F is not 10^-12 F either. A picofarad is 10^-12 F, the small ceramic and stray-capacitance scale.

q: When the charge on the capacitor is increased, the capacitance of the capacitor _____.
e: When the charge on the capacitor is increased, the capacitance of the capacitor remains constant. increases is not remains constant, and decreases is not remains constant either. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field.

q: The capacitance depends on the size, shape, and the nature of the _____ between the two conductors.
e: The capacitance depends on the size, shape, and the nature of the insulator between the two conductors. Put conductor or semiconductor in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. An insulator does not let charge flow freely, so it can separate conductors or protect a live part. A conductor lets charge drift when a potential difference is applied across it.

q: The amount of charge given to a conductor to change its potential by one unit is called the _____ of the conductor.
e: The amount of charge given to a conductor to change its potential by one unit is called the resistance of the conductor. electric capacity is not resistance, and inductance is not resistance either. Resistance opposes current and turns electrical energy into heat. Charge is conserved; it is what a current carries and what a capacitor stores on its plates.

q: Although the capacitance does not depend on Q and V, it depends on the size and the _____ of the capacitor.
e: Although the capacitance does not depend on Q and V, it depends on the size and the shape of the capacitor. Put color or weight in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field.

q: If the potential difference of the capacitor is 1V when it is given a charge 1 C, its capacitance is _____.
e: If the potential difference of the capacitor is 1V when it is given a charge 1 C, its capacitance is 1 C. 1 F and 1 V belong to other processes, not this 1 C case. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field.
